title: Thanks to AI workflows, I built and polished this multiplayer tabletop board game solo in 2 months.
author: Then_Raspberry_6468
selftext:
Two months ago I wanted to take that old 4 Ace horse race card game where people just watch random cards flip, and turn it into an actual board game set inside a museum at night.



Honestly, without AI there is no way I could have pulled this off solo in two months. I handled the game design, rules, and overall look, and used AI coding tools for the heavy Unity C# work, PC and mobile crossplay, automated testing, 10 language translations, and local sound models for the board and UI sound effects.



Since the coding part went so fast, I could spend most of my time just making the game itself more fun. On your turn you flip two cards and pick one, even if both move someone else's horse. The track rules change every race, you pick new perks between rounds, and you unlock new statues by rubbing a coin over scratch tickets.



It is called Suits & Stallions and comes out on Steam, iOS, and Android on December 1. Steam link is in the comments, and I am happy to answer anything about the setup I used.
